meta: Ask AI something and get an answer that's correct but generic, written for anyone? Bit shows two tricks: Role: give AI a role, like a coach for beginners with 20 minutes a day. System prompt: rules for the whole chat.

muc.title: A generic answer
muc.text: Mark asks AI for a workout plan and gets back a long text that's correct but generic, written for anyone.

muc.title: Give AI a role
muc.text: Bit shows the first trick: give it a role. Write: you are a coach for beginners who only have twenty minutes a day. The role helps AI pick the right knowledge and the right way to talk.

muc.title: The clearer the role, the better
muc.text: The more specific the role, the better. "Expert" is vague. "Coach for office workers with back pain" is much clearer.

muc.title: Rules for the whole conversation
muc.text: The second trick: a system prompt, instructions that sit above the whole conversation. For example: answer in five lines at most, and ask me if information is missing. Every question after that, AI follows these rules.

muc.title: You have a system prompt too
muc.text: You don't need to be a programmer to have a system prompt. The custom instructions in Settings, or a Project's instructions, are exactly that, as in videos 27 and 66.

muc.title: A role doesn't replace knowledge
muc.text: Note: giving AI the role of a doctor doesn't make it a doctor. For important matters about health or money, still ask a real person.

muc.title: Write 3 rules for AI
muc.text: Write three rules you want AI to always follow, like be brief, give examples, use a friendly tone, then paste them into custom instructions.
